entities.summary: Vulca of Veii was an Etruscan artist from the town of Veii. The only Etruscan artist mentioned by ancient writers, he worked for the last of the Roman kings, Tarquinius Superbus. He is responsible for creating a terracotta statue of Jupiter and a four-horse chariot for the Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus on the Capitoline Hill, as well as a terracotta statue of Hercules, known as the Hercules Fictilis from its composition. Some have postulated that he also constructred the Apollo of Veii. His statue of Jupiter was reputedly painted with cinnabar and victorious Roman generals would paint their faces red in imitation during their triumphal marches through Rome.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Vulca's terracotta statue of Jupiter and chariot were renowned works that showcased Etruscan artistry and influenced Roman artistic styles. His creations also served as models for later artworks, highlighting the significance of his contributions to the development of Western art.
